<description>
The USDT functional tests currently use BCC to attach eBPF programs to Bitcoin Core’s tracepoints. This requires BCC, matching kernel headers, and elevated BPF permissions, making the tests awkward to run locally and
requiring a privileged container in CI.

Replace the BCC consumers with GDB. Each tested node runs as a debugger child, allowing the tests to enable the real USDT probes and inspect their arguments when execution reaches the probe location. This continues to test
the parts of the USDT interface provided by Bitcoin Core:

- the probe metadata is present and understood;
- the probes can be enabled and are reached in the expected scenarios; and
- their arguments have the expected values, sizes, and lifetimes.

All five tests can run with GDB and `binutils`, without BCC or matching kernel headers. The ASan CI job no longer needs a privileged container and uses `SYS_PTRACE` instead. This also removes the embedded BPF programs from
the tests, reducing their size and maintenance burden. Overall, the change removes roughly 660 lines of test and CI code.

#### Tradeoffs

- These tests no longer exercise the consumer-side eBPF path, including BCC   compilation, kernel BPF verification and loading, uprobe attachment, BPF-side argument decoding, and perf-buffer delivery. Problems confined to
  those components would no longer be detected here.
- LeakSanitizer is disabled for nodes run under GDB because it cannot operate under `ptrace`. Other sanitizer checks remain enabled.

The remaining coverage is focused on Bitcoin Core’s side of the USDT interface. Testing the general BCC, eBPF, and kernel uprobe is left to those consumers and the kernel.
</description>

<commits>
03d302c2c6 test: Capture USDT probes with GDB

Launch traced nodes as GDB children so the existing probe scenarios can
run without BCC, BPF privileges, or matching host kernel headers.

- Copy probe arguments while stopped and drain complete records in the
  test process, including events emitted during node shutdown and
  restart.
- Follow the bitcoin launcher through exec before registering probes.
- Handle a GDB parser failure for GCC byte-register operands in usdt.py.
- Disable LeakSanitizer only for traced children because it cannot
  operate under ptrace; keep other sanitizer checks remain enabled.

e0ef6fd65a ci: Run tracing tests without BPF dependencies

The USDT tests now launch nodes under GDB, so the ASan job no longer needs
BCC, matching host kernel headers, or a privileged container. Install GDB
and binutils and retain SYS_PTRACE for debugger and sanitizer operation.
Remove the host-kernel package refresh and BCC workflow toggle along with
the dependencies they supported.
</commits>

+## Testing tracepoints
+
+The `interface_usdt_*` functional tests use GDB with Python and SystemTap probe
+support, plus `readelf` from binutils. Build with `-DWITH_USDT=ON`, then run:
+
+```sh
+build/test/functional/test_runner.py --filter=interface_usdt
+```
+
+GDB launches each tested node as its child, enables probe semaphores, and copies
+probe arguments before resuming execution. These tests run as an ordinary user
+without BCC, BPF permissions, or kernel headers. The build still needs the USDT
+headers described above. Containers must allow child tracing, for example with
+`--cap-add SYS_PTRACE` in Docker.
+
+LeakSanitizer leak checks are disabled only for the traced nodes because LSan
+cannot run under ptrace. Other sanitizer checks remain enabled.

diff --git a/test/functional/test_framework/usdt.py b/test/functional/test_framework/usdt.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..98cb86a0a5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/functional/test_framework/usdt.py
@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+# Copyright (c) The Bitcoin Core developers
+# Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying
+# file COPYING or http://www.opensource.org/licenses/mit-license.php.
+"""Capture USDT arguments with GDB running the node as its child."""
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+
+class USDT:
+    """Wrap a node before starting it; read() drains captured probe events.
+
+    Probe fields are (name, kind) pairs: integers (i), strings (s), hashes
+    in display order (h), or message bytes (b, length in argument five).
+    GDB copies pointed-to data before resuming the node. Each restart appends
+    to the same event file so shutdown probes remain available to the test.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, node, probes):
+        self.probes = probes
+        self.path = node.datadir_path / "usdt.jsonl"
+        self.path.write_text("")
+        self.offset = 0
+        script = node.datadir_path / "capture.gdb"
+        # The bitcoin launcher execs the daemon; its own ELF has no probes.
+        wrapped = node.binaries.paths.bitcoin_cmd is not None
+        launch = "catch exec\nrun\ndelete breakpoints\n" if wrapped else ""
+        script.write_text(
+            "set pagination off\nset confirm off\nset debuginfod enabled off\n"
+            "set disable-randomization off\n"
+            "set print thread-events off\npython\nimport gdb, os, runpy\n"
+            # LeakSanitizer cannot suspend threads already traced by GDB.
+            "gdb.execute('set environment LSAN_OPTIONS ' + os.environ.get('LSAN_OPTIONS', '') + ':detect_leaks=0')\n"
+            "end\n" + launch + "python\n"
+            f"runpy.run_path({str(Path(__file__).resolve())!r}, "
+            f"init_globals={{'events_path': {str(self.path)!r}, 'probes': {probes!r}}}, run_name='__gdb__')\n"
+            "end\n" + ("continue\n" if wrapped else "run\n")
+        )
+        node.args = ["gdb", "-q", "-nx", "--batch", "--return-child-result", "-x", str(script), "--args", *node.args]
+
+    def read(self):
+        events = []
+        with self.path.open() as stream:
+            stream.seek(self.offset)
+            while line := stream.readline():
+                # Leave an incomplete final record for the next read.
+                if not line.endswith("\n"):
+                    break
+                row = json.loads(line)
+                if "error" in row:
+                    raise AssertionError(row["error"])
+                fields = {}
+                for (name, kind), value in zip(self.probes[row["probe"]], row["args"], strict=True):
+                    fields[name] = bytes.fromhex(value) if kind == "b" else value
+                events.append(SimpleNamespace(probe=row["probe"], **fields))
+                self.offset = stream.tell()
+        return events
+
+    def clear(self):
+        self.read()
+
+
+def record_probes():
+    import gdb  # type: ignore[import]
+    import re
+    import subprocess
+
+    output = open(globals()["events_path"], "a", buffering=1)
+    char_pointer = gdb.lookup_type("char").pointer()
+
+    def read_operand(description):
+        # GDB 17.2 rejects GCC's r8b..r15b names, calling them r8l..r15l.
+        # Read the unmodified ELF operand only for that specific parser error.
+        size, operand = description.split("@", 1)
+        size = int(size)
+        arg_type = gdb.lookup_type(("signed " if size < 0 else "unsigned ") +
+                                   {1: "char", 2: "short", 4: "int", 8: "long long"}[abs(size)])
+        if operand.startswith("%"):
+            register = re.sub(r"^(r(?:[89]|1[0-5]))b$", r"\1l", operand[1:])
+            value = gdb.parse_and_eval(f"${register}")
+        elif operand.startswith("$"):
+            value = gdb.Value(int(operand[1:], 0))
+        else:
+            address = re.fullmatch(r"(-?\d*)\(%(\w+)\)", operand)
+            if address is None:
+                raise AssertionError(f"Unsupported USDT operand: {description}")
+            offset, register = address.groups()
+            value = gdb.Value(int(gdb.parse_and_eval(f"${register}")) + int(offset or 0)).cast(arg_type.pointer()).dereference()
+        return int(value.cast(arg_type))
+
+    class Probe(gdb.Breakpoint):
+        def __init__(self, name, fields):
+            super().__init__(f"-probe-stap {name}", internal=True)
+            self.probe_name = name
+            self.fields = fields
+            self.operands = None
+
+        def stop(self):
+            try:
+                try:
+                    count = int(gdb.parse_and_eval("$_probe_argc"))
+                    raw = [int(gdb.parse_and_eval(f"$_probe_arg{i}")) for i in range(count)]
+                except gdb.error as error:
+                    if not re.match(r"Invalid register name .r(?:[89]|1[0-5])b", str(error)):
+                        raise
+                    if self.operands is None:
+                        notes = subprocess.check_output(["readelf", "--notes", gdb.current_progspace().filename], text=True)
+                        layouts = {f"{provider}:{name}": args.split() for provider, name, args in
+                                   re.findall(r"Provider: (\w+)\n\s+Name: (\w+).*?Arguments: ([^\n]*)", notes, re.S)}
+                        self.operands = layouts[self.probe_name]
+                    raw = [read_operand(operand) for operand in self.operands]
+                    count = len(raw)
+                if count != len(self.fields):
+                    raise AssertionError(f"{self.probe_name}: expected {len(self.fields)} arguments, got {count}")
+                args = []
+                for (_, field), value in zip(self.fields, raw):
+                    if field == "s":
+                        value = gdb.Value(value).cast(char_pointer).string(encoding="utf-8")
+                    elif field == "h":
+                        value = bytes(gdb.selected_inferior().read_memory(value, 32))[::-1].hex()
+                    elif field == "b":
+                        message_size = raw[4]
+                        # Empty messages, e.g. verack, have no bytes to read.
+                        # GDB's read_memory requires a strictly positive size.
+                        if message_size == 0:
+                            value = ""
+                        else:
+                            value = bytes(gdb.selected_inferior().read_memory(value, message_size)).hex()
+                    args.append(value)
+                output.write(json.dumps({"probe": self.probe_name, "args": args}) + "\n")
+                return False
+            except Exception as error:
+                message = f"{self.probe_name}: {error}"
+                output.write(json.dumps({"error": message}) + "\n")
+                gdb.write(message + "\n", gdb.STDERR)
+                gdb.execute("quit 1")
+
+    for name, fields in globals()["probes"].items():
+        Probe(name, fields)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__gdb__":
+    record_probes()
